active.title: One-line bootstrap: uvx dadaia-workspace init <dir> [--repo <url>] scaffolds a full workspace
active.description: Adoption blocker #1: today a first workspace takes 7 stages (install, init, context create/alive/bind, doctor, panel, install-hook) while every tool above 20k stars installs in one line. One command, run by the operator with a VALID directory name (required), scaffolds the whole workspace state: root law, harness projections, .dadaia/ zones, venv, hooks. Multi-repo stays the foundation: repos live INSIDE the workspace under repos/<slug>/, never as a monorepo; the minimal case is one workspace with one repo. The first repo is OPTIONAL at bootstrap (--repo <url> clones it, creates its context ALIVE and binds the shell in the same step); without a URL the operator is oriented to repos/ as the place of work and to `dadaia context create/alive` for the first project. No verb of the context lifecycle is visible before the second project.
active.provenance: operator ruling 2026-09-18 (competitive report 'dadaia-workspace: diferencial e panorama competitivo'): five urgencies before any public launch

active.description: Adoption channel: distribution in 2026 is the marketplace, and the Claude marketplace alone is not viable because we support Codex and Kimi Code. Publish the skills that survive without the workspace (dd-grill-me, dd-bug-resolution, dd-code-review three-axis, dd-test-stewardship) as one skills repo in the standard layout, registered on the Anthropic marketplace (claude-plugins-official / claude-community), the Codex marketplace (`codex marketplace add`) and installable by `npx skills add`; each skill names dadaia-workspace as the place where the full lifecycle lives. Complements plugin-packaging-and-skill-evals (the whole AI surface as one Claude plugin): this entry is the harness-neutral entry door.

active.title: Panel: keep only what no harness dashboard has, define the rest with the operator
active.description: Panel + telemetry are 8.6k LOC (17% of production) and 17 bugs for a surface that codex agents, Copilot Agent HQ and Cursor Agents Window now cover generically. Two things are unique and the operator values them: the cross-harness view per project with cost per model, and managing sub-agents and the model/effort each one gets (the agent_model_policy editor, the only governance UI). To define calmly before picking: (a) is a CLI verb the better home for the policy — `dadaia agents list` / `dadaia agents model <agent> --model <id> --effort <level>` writing agent_model_policy.json and reprojecting, scriptable and diff-able, with the panel as a read-only view; (b) delete what is generic (Servers tab together with the dev-server registry; anything the native dashboards show); (c) keep or drop the loopback web UI itself once the two unique functions live in the CLI. If nothing unique remains in the UI, the panel is deleted, not trimmed.

active.title: SDD ledger verbs move from the CLI into skill-local scripts/ (stdlib, path-parameterized)
active.description: Structural cause named by the bug history: every specs/ ledger contract lives in three places that drift separately — the CLI verb that writes, the doctor rule that validates, the skill that instructs (specs 44 bugs, backlog 18, bugs 18, spec_context 48; 'doctor' in 102 titles, 'release' in 56). Every verb also drags context resolution, venv guard and session binding, which have nothing to do with writing one JSON line. Decision: what touches only specs/ (bugs, backlog, release, audit, ADR) becomes a minimal stdlib script under the owning skill's scripts/ (Agent Skills standard name; never python/), parameterized by the specs/ path, no import of dadaia_workspace, one file per verb, <= ~150 lines, tested by the lib's pytest from public/skills/<skill>/scripts/. Each script is the ONE writer and the ONE validator of its ledger (append|resolve|check); dadaia doctor calls check instead of re-implementing the schema. What touches .dadaia/ (init, context, projection, hooks, git chokepoints, workspace doctor) stays in the CLI, which shrinks to workspace operations; dd-cli-library shrinks with it. HANDEDIT/governance-event telemetry for specs/ ledgers is deleted (a WARNING nobody acts on). Contract test: every fix: line of every doctor names a script or verb that exists. Gate for one-line-bootstrap and standalone-skills-distribution: a skill is only distributable alone when it no longer calls the workspace CLI. Skill split by behavior-map: 11 canonical skills keep coming from the lib and gain scripts/ (manager-orchestration, gitflow-default, handoff-emitter, backlog-definition, release-definition, release-implementation, audit-project, spec-navigator, bug-registration, bug-resolution, cli-library); 7 generic ones (grill-me, codebase-design, code-review, domain-modeling, test-stewardship, architecture-survey, ai-eng-knowhow) leave dadaia-workspace for the marketplace repo.

active.description: Value scale class 14 (roles and orchestration) carries the second-strongest negative signal in the community: coordination tax, subagents starving for context, orchestrators producing garbage. Operator verdict: keep only PM (intake, dispatch, backlog), engineer (all production code and tests) and reviewer (the verdict). Architecture, security, QA, product-engineering, auditing and AI-engineering stop being staffed agents with dispatch bands and become REVIEW LENSES: named axes the reviewer (and the engineer before handing off) applies from a skill, each lens with its checklist and its verdict line, no separate context, no handoff between personas. Ownership table in DADAIA.md section 2 shrinks to three rows; behavior-map and registry drop six personas; the security push verdict is one lens of the reviewer.

active.title: Doctor without scores: keep the rules, run in CI, fail on dead references and superseded decisions
active.description: Value scale class 13: nobody in the community asks for a compliance percentage; they ask 'fail my CI when a rule points at a superseded decision'. Operator verdict: remove the compliance(<section>) N/M (P%) and compliance(total) lines and the canonical-count scoring machinery; a doctor run is a list of findings and an exit code, nothing else. Keep every rule. Add the two checks the community names: a memory atom, rule or skill citing an ADR that is superseded, and a citation of a path or symbol that no longer exists, both errors. Wire the doctor as a CI job on every push. Coordinates with sdd-verbs-to-skill-scripts (the ledgers section delegates to skill scripts' check).

active.title: Spec Context Project is the heart: audit its bug history, rename to main-repo/associated-repos, harden the paradigm
active.description: Operator verdict: the foundation stays and must improve. The paradigm that gave birth to dadaia-workspace: open an agent in ONE folder (the workspace) and manage projects that live in repos inside it, with skills, rules, AGENTS.md and the .dadaia/ runtime OUTSIDE every repo; canonical rules that steer away from slop; and the Spec Context Project, where projects are created and managed, each project multi-repo, the main repo hosting specs/. Multi-project where each project can be multi-repo, never a monorepo. Work: (1) a bug-history audit of the spec_context surface (160 of 512 records touch context, bind, session or presence; 8 context deciders before ADR 0003) naming the weak points and the structural fixes; (2) rename the vocabulary everywhere (CLI, JSON state, docs, memory, glossary): repo_slug -> main-repo, associated_repos -> associated-repos, and 'main repo' is defined as the repo where specs/ lives; (3) freeze the context surface: no new verb, no new state, single-repo is the degenerate case of multi-repo; (4) write the paradigm as the first page of the docs. Complements one-line-bootstrap (which owns init and the first-run path) and delete-advisory-presence.
